name: ELEVATE Idea2PoC Grant-in-Aid (General, Shakti, Aspire and Minorities calls)
provider: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka, through Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS)
amountText: One-time grant-in-aid of up to ₹50 lakh, released in milestone tranches. If you apply to several tracks in the same call, one pitch is judged and the total is still capped at ₹50 lakh.
duration: Paid in tranches against agreed milestones; the second tranche is released after your assigned K-tech Innovation Hub or Centre of Excellence reviews progress
timeToMoney: Roughly 4–6 months from the application deadline to winners being announced (ELEVATE 2025 applications closed 17 Sep 2025; winners were felicitated 17 Jan 2026), then the first tranche after documents and agreement
deadline: ELEVATE 2026 (General, Shakti, Aspire) closed 15 Jul 2026, results awaited. ELEVATE Minorities 2026 is open 13 Oct–13 Nov 2026 (5 pm IST)
oneLiner: Karnataka's flagship no-equity grant of up to ₹50 lakh to turn an early idea into a working product.
what: ELEVATE is a one-time grant from the Karnataka government for early-stage startups registered in the state. The money is meant for building a prototype or proof-of-concept, early market development and scale-up. Winners also get mentoring and subsidised incubation at government-backed K-tech Innovation Hubs and Centres of Excellence. Calls run under several tracks: General, Shakti (women-led), Aspire (outside Bengaluru Urban) and Minorities; SC/ST founders have a separate track, ELEVATE Unnati.
who: A Private Limited company, One Person Company, LLP or registered partnership firm incorporated in Karnataka (the 2026 calls also accept co-operative societies)
Not more than 10 years old from the date of incorporation on the cut-off date
Turnover has never crossed ₹100 crore in any year (ELEVATE 2025 rule; the Minorities 2026 call allows up to ₹200 crore)
Working on a new or improved product, service or process with potential to create jobs or wealth
Shakti track: women hold at least 51% ownership. Aspire track: registered outside Bengaluru Urban

Minorities track: one or more directors/partners from a notified minority community (Muslim, Buddhist, Jain, Sikh, Parsi) together hold at least 51% equity and have a digital minority certificate with an RD number
notFor: Startups (or their directors/partners) that won ELEVATE, Idea2PoC, a state Grand Challenge or any Karnataka government grant in the last 3 years
Subsidiaries, franchises, resellers, group companies, demerged units and government/PPP projects
Section 8 companies, trusts, societies, associations and other non-profits
Founders who only have Udyam/MSME, GST, trade licence or shop registration: these are not accepted as incorporation proof
Companies registered outside Karnataka (look at ELEVATE NxT instead if you are deep-tech)
why: It is a grant, not a loan or equity: you give up no shares and repay nothing
Up to ₹50 lakh is several times larger than most state idea-stage grants in India
Being an ELEVATE winner is a credibility signal; more than 1,230 startups have been backed since 2017
You are plugged into a K-tech hub for mentoring, plus state policy reimbursements for patents, marketing, GST and quality certification
howItWorks: You apply online on the department's ELEVATE portal during an open call. Applications go through four stages: eligibility and document check, pitch-deck review, an in-person multi-city pitching round and a Grand Finale. Juries drawn from NASSCOM, TiE, IESA, ABLE, VC firms and academia score each pitch out of 100 (novelty 30, business model 30, socio-economic impact 20, team 10, budget plan 10). The ELEVATE/Idea2PoC Evaluation Committee, chaired by the Secretary of the department, fixes the cut-off score (it was an average of 75.33 for ELEVATE 2024) and the amount each winner gets. KITS signs an agreement with you and pays in tranches; ₹25,000 plus GST from the grant is earmarked for your assigned K-tech hub's mentoring and milestone-review services.

steps.title: Pick your track
steps.detail: Decide between General, Shakti (51%+ women ownership), Aspire (outside Bengaluru Urban), Minorities, or Unnati (SC/ST). You may apply to more than one track in a call, but the total grant stays capped at ₹50 lakh.

steps.title: Get your paperwork ready
steps.detail: Incorporation certificate, MoA or partnership deed, a startup affidavit notarised on ₹100 e-stamp paper (second party: Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society), and the pitch deck in the portal's template. Track-specific certificates must be digital with an RD number.

steps.title: Register and apply online
steps.detail: Create an account on the ELEVATE portal, choose the call, fill every field and upload documents before the deadline. Nothing can be edited after you submit, so check carefully. You get an ELEVATE ID to track the application.

steps.title: Clear screening
steps.detail: The department checks eligibility and documents, then reviewers assess your pitch deck. Missing or wrong documents lead to rejection at any stage.

steps.title: Pitch in person
steps.detail: Shortlisted startups pitch to a jury at the multi-city pitching round. You need a minimum score (60 marks in the 2026 calls) to reach the Grand Finale; the founder who meets the track's ownership rule must attend.

steps.title: Grand Finale and selection
steps.detail: Finalists pitch again; the Evaluation Committee sets the cut-off and decides each winner's grant amount.

steps.title: Sign up and get the first tranche
steps.detail: Sign the agreement with KITS, join your assigned K-tech Innovation Hub or CoE, and receive the first tranche. Later tranches follow milestone reviews.

name: ELEVATE NxT DeepTech Grant-in-Aid
provider: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka, through Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS)
amountText: Up to ₹1 crore grant-in-aid per startup, released against milestones (part of a ₹150 crore deep-tech programme announced in January 2026)
duration: Milestone-based tranches; winners are mapped to K-tech partners for mentoring
timeToMoney: Not yet established: the programme is new. Applications close 13 Nov 2026, followed by jury rounds and a Grand Finale; expect several months
deadline: Current call open 13 Oct 2026 (9 am) to 13 Nov 2026 (5 pm IST)
oneLiner: A Karnataka grant of up to ₹1 crore for deep-tech startups from anywhere in India, if winners move their registered office to Karnataka.
what: ELEVATE NxT is the deep-tech version of Karnataka's ELEVATE grant. It funds startups whose products rest on real science or hard engineering, with patent potential, such as AI, quantum, semiconductors, space, robotics and advanced biotech. It is open to startups registered anywhere in India, but winners from outside Karnataka must shift their registered office to Karnataka. The grant is milestone-based and comes with mentoring.
who: Private Limited company, registered partnership firm, LLP, or state/multi-state co-operative society, incorporated anywhere in India
Independent entity: not a subsidiary, spin-off or internal division of another company
Within 20 years of incorporation, and turnover below ₹300 crore in every financial year
At least two people in the founding or core team
Technology at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 3 to 8, i.e. at least an experimental proof-of-concept and up to a qualified system
Rooted in advanced technology with high technical complexity and strong intellectual-property potential, solving a real problem
notFor: Startups that received any ELEVATE grant in the last 3 years
Software or service businesses without a genuine deep-tech core (the first jury round exists to screen these out)
Out-of-state winners unwilling to move their registered office to Karnataka within 4 months of results (the application is then treated as rejected)
Founders planning to change ownership terms to their own advantage during the project
why: ₹1 crore without dilution is rare for deep-tech at the prototype-to-pilot stage, where VCs are cautious
Open to all of India, unlike most state grants
Anonymised first round means a strong idea can win without a famous team
Plugs you into Karnataka's deep-tech ecosystem and K-tech partners
howItWorks: Applications go through the department portal. After an eligibility check, startups get anonymised IDs and two domain-expert jurors review a 2-slide anonymised 'qualification' deck to decide whether the startup is truly deep-tech; at least one juror must agree for it to proceed. Qualified startups pitch a second, non-anonymised business-model deck in person; a score of at least 60 is needed to reach the Grand Finale. Final scores weight Round 1 at 40% and the Grand Finale at 60%, across research depth (20), technical foundation (20), commercialisation (20), socio-economic effect (20), team (10) and grant-use plan (10). Winners are approved by the ELEVATE Evaluation Committee chaired by the Secretary and paid in milestone tranches.

steps.detail: Be honest about your Technology Readiness Level (3–8) and write a 200-word justification of why you are deep-tech.

steps.title: Build two decks
steps.detail: Deck 1: max 2 slides, fully anonymised (no company name, logo, founder names, address or patent numbers). Deck 2: business model in the portal's template, used at the in-person round.

steps.title: Collect documents
steps.detail: Incorporation certificate, MoA/LLP deed, CA-certified FY 2025–26 revenue certificate, CA-attested shareholding pattern, patent certificate if any, and an affidavit notarised on ₹100 e-stamp paper naming KITS.

steps.detail: Register, choose the ELEVATE NxT call, fill the form and upload everything before 13 Nov 2026, 5 pm IST. Incomplete applications are rejected.

steps.title: Jury qualification round
steps.detail: Two jurors review your anonymised Deck 1. If both say you are not deep-tech, you are out.

steps.title: In-person pitch and Grand Finale
steps.detail: Pitch Deck 2 in person (minimum 60 marks to advance), then pitch again at the Grand Finale.

steps.title: Relocate if needed and receive tranches
steps.detail: Out-of-state winners must move their registered office to Karnataka within 4 months. Sign the agreement and receive milestone-linked tranches.

what: ELEVATE Unnati is the ELEVATE grant reserved for startups where founders from Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe communities own most of the company. The Evaluation Committee chaired by the Secretary approves winners and grant amounts. The grant is funded through the Social Welfare Department's Scheduled Castes Sub-Plan and Tribal Sub-Plan, and KITS releases it in milestone tranches.

name: KSUM Innovation Grant: Idea Grant (including Student Innovator Idea Grant)
provider: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), Government of Kerala
amountText: Up to ₹3 lakh for startups/innovators; up to ₹2 lakh for student innovators (paid through the college IEDC)
duration: Two tranches: usually 50% first, the rest after a progress report and utilisation certificate (grants under ₹50,000 are paid in one go)
timeToMoney: Several weeks to a few months after an Idea Day pitch: grantees are listed within about two weeks, then documents and an agreement must be completed before the first tranche (KSUM does not publish a fixed timeline)
deadline: Calls announced on the KSUM website and social media; no dated call was visible in October 2026
oneLiner: Kerala's entry-level grant of up to ₹3 lakh to turn a tech idea into a first working prototype.
what: The Idea Grant is the first step of KSUM's Innovation Grant ladder. It pays for proof-of-concept work, prototyping, testing and validation for innovative technology products. You can apply before forming a company, but you must incorporate (Pvt Ltd, LLP or OPC) and get a KSUM Unique ID before any money is released. Students can get up to ₹2 lakh through their college's Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development Centre (IEDC).
who: Innovators or startups at the ideation, design or proof-of-concept stage
Innovators based in or outside Kerala may apply; a KSUM Unique ID is not needed to apply
Before disbursal you need a company (Pvt Ltd, LLP or OPC) and a KSUM Unique ID; KSUM's own guide says selected innovators must register the company in Kerala
Only innovative technology-based products are considered
Student innovators studying in Kerala can apply for the ₹2 lakh student version via their IEDC
notFor: Service projects, agencies and non-technology businesses
Anyone who applied for the same grant in the last 3 months or already received it
People wanting to pay founder salaries, rent or buy land, buildings or costly equipment (not allowed)
Founders unwilling to incorporate and register with KSUM before disbursal
why: Free money at the riskiest stage, when angels rarely invest
Pitching at an Idea Day forces you to sharpen problem, customer and solution
It is the first rung: later Productisation, Market Acceleration and Scale-up grants build on it (up to ₹15 lakh in total)

howItWorks: KSUM opens calls on its website (the guidelines say at least once a year or on demand) and scouts ideas through events such as the Kerala Innovation Drive. Applications are screened by KSUM staff; shortlisted applicants pitch their idea and fund-use plan at an Idea Day before an expert committee, which scores team, product innovation, marketing, financials and grant-use plan. The CEO/Chairman of KSUM approves the list. After you submit documents and sign an agreement at a KSUM office, the grant is paid in milestone tranches; you must bring 10% of the grant as your own contribution (margin money) from the second tranche.
